3 The story · A história

The Silva Family

A Família Silva

Read slowly. Every sentence with have/has is a clue to answer the claims below.

Leia devagar. Cada frase com have/has é uma pista pra responder as suposições mais abaixo.

The Full Story
0:00

It's Sunday, and the Silva family has lunch in the backyard every week. Alice and Joe are the grandparents, and they have two children: Julia and David. Julia is married to Mark, and they have two kids, Ben and Nina. Ben is ten years old, and he has a new bicycle. Nina is seven, and she doesn't have a bicycle — she has a skateboard instead.

David is Julia's brother, and he's married to Sofia. David and Sofia have one daughter, and her name is Zoe. Zoe has long brown hair, and today she has her guitar with her. Ben and Nina are Zoe's cousins. Alice and Joe have a small dog, and his name is Max. Max has a red collar, and he's very calm today.

The Silva family's house has a big backyard and a swimming pool. The house doesn't have a garage, but it has a long table under the trees. Every Sunday, the family has lunch together at that table. After lunch, Ben and Nina usually play near the pool. Zoe often plays her guitar for everyone after lunch.

Neural English · EIC — Escola de Idiomas e Cultura
The Full Story
Como montar a pergunta
A regra
he / she / it → Does + sujeito + have + resto + ?
I / you / we / they → Do + sujeito + have + resto + ?
Exemplos do texto
Ben has a new bicycle. → Does Ben have a new bicycle?
Alice and Joe have a small dog. → Do Alice and Joe have a small dog?
The house has a swimming pool. → Does the house have a swimming pool?
Cuidado
O verbo principal é sempre have na pergunta — nunca "has", mesmo com he/she/it. O "s" já está em does.
